newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia, HK to cooperate on criminal fugitives.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia, HK to cooperate on criminal fugitives.

text.p: Cambodia has promised to help Hong Kong police track down fugitives wanted for crimes in the British colony, a Hong Kong police officer said on Thursday.

"They're very happy to initiate cooperation with Hong Kong and discuss cases where Hong Kong residents committed crimes and are believed to have fled to Cambodia," senior inspector Martin Richardson of the Organised Crime and Triad Bureau said.
Richardson said the police had focused on a few specific cases, including people wanted for murder and armed robbery, with local Interpol representatives.
"The Cambodians have said they will look out for these people," he said.
He said Hong Kong was ready to forward details, including photographs, of wanted criminals to local authorities.
Interpol officials believe Cambodia, with its weak law enforcement system, has become a haven for criminals on the run from police in their home countries.
Richardson flew into Phnom Penh on Tuesday to help local police probe an international illegal immigration ring.
Cambodian officials said two men were likely to be charged in the near future for immigration offences. Cambodia has not enacted yet legislation covering human trafficking.
The police had promised to deport the men to Hong Kong after their terms had been served, said Richardson, noting that the two countries had no extradition agreement.
The two detained men, Chan Hak-so and Chan Yui-chun, were arrested on December 25 as suspected members of a smuggling ring after police found 78 ethnic Chinese hiding in a Phnom Penh villa.

The two Hong Kong men are suspected of leading a crime syndicate thought to have illegally moved large numbers of Chinese migrants, mostly from mainland China, to the United States, South America, Europe and Africa.
Chan Hak-so is a fugitive from Hong Kong who fled to Cambodia last November after jumping bail on passport violation charges.

Richardson said the Hong Kong men had given them documents, bank details and lists of overseas contacts in Europe, North America, the Caribbean and South America. "They provided us with some information which we need to follow up on," he added.
